title: PUBG Asia Stars 2026 — Himass / TanVuu Case
purpose: Preserve a multilingual, source-traceable record of the controversy and distinguish verified facts from official claims, party positions, testimony, allegations and analysis.
core_question: Even if a competitive-integrity violation occurred, do the rules, organizer instructions, event design, investigation process and disclosed reasoning adequately explain and justify permanent account bans and lifetime exclusion from official PUBG esports?
important_distinctions: Information appearing in a player's chat is not automatically the same as the player deliberately seeking it.
Seeing outside information is not automatically the same as materially using it in tactical decisions.
A violation finding and the proportionality of the chosen sanction are separate questions.
An official statement proves that the organization made that statement; it does not automatically make every underlying factual assertion independently verified.
An allegation against Soopi is not proof of cheating; equally, the absence of a sanction does not by itself disclose the full investigative basis.
do_not_claim_without_more_evidence: Do not state that the organizer definitely permitted stream sniping until the alleged authorization is sourced.
Do not state that KRAFTON pre-planned a setup against the Vietnamese players.
Do not state that Soopi cheated or used aimbot.
Do not state that a lawsuit has been filed unless a filing or official statement confirms it.
Do not state that community support counters represent verified unique individuals without an auditable methodology.
